newsitem.title: GERMANY: Meeting on Zaire relief continues into weekend.
newsitem.headline: Meeting on Zaire relief continues into weekend.

text.p: The coordinator of a prospective multinational military mission to help Zaire's refugee crisis said on Friday that a planning meeting working out options for action would continue through the weekend.

"By the end of the weekend I would hope we will have developed a full slate of options," Lieutenant-General Maurice Baril of Canada, which is coordinating the U.N.-authorised mission, told a news conference held at U.S. European Command headquarters in Stuttgart, Germany.

Baril refused to be drawn on how many troops, if any, such a mission might require, but he said there appeared to be between 100,000 and 250,000 refugees "in the conditions we are talking about" requiring help.

A major problem for nations wanting to help has been the fluidity of the situation in eastern Zaire, where hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees have been displaced by a conflict pitting Rwandan-backed Zairean Tutsi rebels against Zairean government forces and Rwandan Hutu militias.
Baril said estimates presented at the meeting of the total number of displaced refugees in eastern Zaire ranged between 100,000 and 500,000.
"The mandate we have is to open a (relief) corridor to those who really need it," he said. "We're not here to feed and transport them, but to open the corridor."
